steps.summary: first to move: control.attitude_setpoint[roll] at 8.66 s, vehicle.velocity[x] at 8.82 s, actuator.output[ch[3]] at 8.875 s

result.headline: No control fault shown: roll deviations follow commanded setpoint steps; only start-up warnings and flat airspeed/yaw-rate channels stand out.
result.explanation: Roll, pitch and yaw loops show no onset of a persistent change or frozen output. Roll divergences coincide with setpoint steps and recover. Start-up warnings and a flat airspeed channel remain unexplained.

evidence.quote: CHANGE control.attitude_setpoint[roll] at t=9.337 s: 44.29 -> 24.67 deg (step -19.62, 1961.6x its usual variation)
evidence.shows: A roll setpoint step of about 20 deg was commanded; the roll divergences at lines 72-73 follow it. Roll error is a response to the command, not an independent fault.
Roll tracking error stays at about 1-2.5 deg through the whole run, with no lasting degradation after any candidate time.
The pitch loop tracks normally throughout.

evidence.quote: CONSTANT vehicle.airspeed = 0 for the whole recording (529 samples)
evidence.shows: Airspeed is 0 for the whole recording while ground velocity is non-zero: the airspeed sensor is not reporting or not logged. It is not a change at an onset.

evidence.quote: EVENT t=0.896 s controller.event[mavros: System] mavros: System: ERROR: Sensor helth
evidence.shows: A start-up sensor-health error and a low-voltage warning at t=0.896 s. Nothing changed later that points back to them.

checked.result: Only two events, both at t=0.896 s (low voltage warning, sensor health error); none during the flight.

checked.check: Sequence around the roll step at 8.5-12 s
checked.result: The roll setpoint left its baseline first (8.66 s), then velocity, the actuators on ch3-5 (8.875 s), then measured roll (9.609 s). The cause precedes the response, which is consistent with a commanded manoeuvre.

No series froze. Roll tracking error went from 1.911 to 4.001 deg (ratio 2.09) as the setpoint stepped, and pitch and yaw tracking did not worsen. Throttle changed by about 10 points and the roll actuators moved.

checked.check: Evidence-sheet lines 22-76: CONSTANT, ROLE, SHIFT, tracking
checked.result: The constant channels are ch0, ch6, ch7, airspeed and yaw_rate. The roll divergences are short, with a largest peak error of 9.923 deg, and recover. Yaw error is a roughly constant offset (typical 93.724 deg) all run.

effects.quote: TRACKING vehicle.attitude[roll] diverged from its setpoint from t=9.737 to 9.96 s (peak |error| 9.923 deg)
effects.why: Follows the commanded roll step at 9.337 s; normal transient lag after a setpoint step.

effects.quote: TRACKING vehicle.attitude[roll] diverged from its setpoint from t=10.152 to 10.606 s (peak |error| 7.899 deg)
effects.why: The same step response, which recovers; measured roll stepped at 10.457 s (line 61).

effects.quote: TRACKING vehicle.attitude[roll] diverged from its setpoint from t=17.275 to 17.923 s (peak |error| 7.775 deg)
effects.why: Short transient that recovers; the roll tracking error stays at 1-2.5 deg in later stretches.

next_action.action: Confirm airspeed sensor logging and the yaw reference frame offset
next_action.why: Settles whether the flat airspeed and the large constant yaw offset are logging or frame artefacts or real sensor faults that this data cannot show.
how: Check the airspeed (pitot) sensor, its wiring and the logging configuration for this flight
Check the yaw setpoint frame against the attitude yaw frame (e.g. magnetic vs true heading) in the autopilot configuration
Compare with another flight of UAV-19 logged with the same configuration

outcomes.label: Logging or frame configuration artefact
outcomes.means: The flat channels and yaw offset are not hardware faults; no control fault is shown.

outcomes.label: Real airspeed or heading sensor fault
outcomes.means: A sensor-health problem existed, consistent with the start-up error; it was not visible in the roll loop.
outcomes.then: Reassess the sensor-health event and request the pre-flight log

unknowns: Whether the 0 airspeed and 0 yaw_rate are real sensor faults or just not logged on this vehicle.
What caused the 'Sensor helth' error and low-voltage warning at t=0.896 s; the recording starts there.

already_answered.question: Did a control fault occur, and when?
already_answered.answer: No loop shows a lasting change at any onset. The roll deviations at 9.7-10.6 s follow the setpoint step at 9.337 s and recover.
already_answered.quote: CHANGE control.attitude_setpoint[roll] at t=9.337 s: 44.29 -> 24.67 deg (step -19.62, 1961.6x its usual variation)

already_answered.question: Which control loop would be affected?
already_answered.answer: Roll is the only loop with transient divergences. ch1/ch2 serve pitch (lines 29-30), and ch3-5 move with roll but do not freeze.
already_answered.quote: ROLE actuator.output[ch[1]] follows control.attitude_setpoint[pitch] (correlation -0.774 over the recording): it serves that loop

unobservable.fact: Whether the airspeed sensor is physically fitted and working
unobservable.why_it_matters: A real sensor fault would explain the start-up sensor-health error; a missing sensor would not.
unobservable.how_to_observe: Inspect the pitot tube and sensor wiring; read the airspeed in the ground-station log with the sensor blown on.

hypotheses.claim: Roll deviations are the normal response to commanded setpoint steps; no lasting change at any onset.
hypotheses.because: The setpoint stepped before the response, nothing froze, and tracking stays at 1-2.5 deg in every stretch.
They moved after the setpoint and recovered; ch4 and ch5 are identical and none froze. Observed only as commanded outputs.

hypotheses.claim: A sensor fault exists (airspeed constant 0; 'Sensor helth' error at start-up).
hypotheses.because: The flat airspeed channel and the start-up error are real but no flight-time change followed.
The warning appears once at t=0.896 s, and no later change in the actuators or roll tracking is tied to it.

events.what: Low voltage warning and sensor health error at start-up
events.why: Both at t=0.896 s; nothing later points back to them.

events.what: Roll setpoint steps of about 17-20 deg
events.why: Commanded manoeuvres, with measured roll following.

events.what: Short roll tracking divergences after setpoint steps
events.why: Transient lag after steps, which recovers.

events.what: Constant channels (ch0, ch6, ch7, airspeed, yaw_rate)
events.why: Flat for the whole recording, so either unused or not reporting.

result.lesson: No earlier cases are available in the workspace.
result.reuse_when: A vehicle with large commanded roll steps and a 0.9 s start-up sensor-health warning shows short roll divergences that recover; compare with the setpoint timing before suspecting an actuator.
